reviewerSelfCorrection: This is the third consecutive artifact where Codex found a blocker I did not, and the pattern in my misses is now legible enough to name. RB-DR005-CX-01 is real and I confirmed it from v1's own bytes before looking at v2: P-005-2 described Operational metadata as 'Host-local, rebuildable'. DR-124's governing enumeration in file 04 carries four state classes, of which Rebuildable cache/index and Operational metadata are distinct and carry opposite rules — the cache class 'May be discarded/rebuilt', while Operational metadata is 'Journaled/redacted/bounded; backup/purge scope disclosed; never a peer evidence writer'. Calling operational metadata rebuildable collapses two classes whose separation is the point of DR-124, and it is wrong on the merits for the specific asset the clause names: a doctor invocation audit record is not regenerable from later state. In my v1 review I checked whether each bound was substantive rather than formal and satisfied myself that it was; what I did not do was check the taxonomy claim inside the bound against the enumeration that governs it. That is the same shape as my two prior misses — at v6 of the host-effect contract I checked whether two members were well-founded but not whether they were typed, and at v7 I checked types but not whether the discriminator predicates came from one domain. In each case I verified that a claim had a real referent and did not verify that the claim conformed to the referent's own structure. This round I read file 04's four state classes first and compared the bounds against them.
summary: The repair is exact and it is grounded rather than asserted. P-005-2 now reads 'Host-local and non-authoritative. Journaled/redacted/bounded; backup/purge scope disclosed; never a peer evidence writer and not a grant journal. Not rebuildable.' The first clause is file 04's operational-metadata rule quoted verbatim — I compared it against the register's own table. It adds the reason the class cannot be rebuildable, that a doctor invocation audit record 'is a report-integrity obligation and is not regenerable from later state', and it fences the neighbouring class explicitly: 'Rebuildability stays on P-005-1's cache/index class only.' P-005-1 retains 'May be deleted and regenerated', matching file 04's cache rule, so the two classes are now separate and each carries its own governing text. Everything I verified at v1 is intact, and the change set is confined to the repair, the pin refresh and the version bump.

whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: 3b50bcf15e207b698283cb51e77335bceaf46f053f961f0de2b9b8d20982b809 both times. No drift.

State classes are not collapsed, checked against the governing enumeration rather than within the artifact. File 04's state-class table gives Operational metadata the rule 'Journaled/redacted/bounded; backup/purge scope disclosed; never a peer evidence writer' and Rebuildable cache/index the rule 'May be discarded/rebuilt; provenance and corruption tests prove no authority or hidden input'. P-005-2 now carries the former verbatim plus 'Not rebuildable'; P-005-1 carries the latter's substance. The classes are distinct in the artifact exactly as they are distinct in the register.

The reason given for non-rebuildability is sound and specific, not a formula. 'Doctor's invocation audit record is a report-integrity obligation and is not regenerable from later state' identifies why the class differs rather than merely asserting that it does, and it connects to the report-integrity thread the host-effect contract carries at its process-death clause.

P-005-4 is not a counterexample: it describes host-local working storage for one invocation as 'Ephemeral or rebuildable', which is a property of invocation-scoped scratch rather than a DR-124 class claim, so it does not reintroduce the collapse.

verdictNote: ACCEPT, zero findings. The repair does the thing that makes a fix checkable rather than assertable: it quotes the governing rule from file 04 instead of paraphrasing it, so a reviewer can compare two texts rather than judge a characterization. I have recorded, for the third consecutive round, a blocker I did not find, together with the common shape of the three misses — verifying that a claim has a real referent without verifying that it conforms to the referent's own structure — and the method change it argues for, which I applied here by reading the four state classes before reading the bounds.
